title: Cascade Highway Transfer Point
event: A landslide closes a mountain highway used for regional food and medical deliveries.
why: Mountain highways connect coastal and inland communities. When one closes, deliveries may have to travel much farther on routes with less capacity.
how: Traffic queues near the closure, trucks consume more fuel on detours, and limited alternate roads receive more vehicles than normal.
when: The risk grows during prolonged rain, rapid snowmelt, wildfire damage, or winter storms because slopes and alternate routes may already be stressed.
where: The first effects appear near the closed highway and then spread to distribution centers, clinics, stores, farms, and communities along the detour.

keyTerms.definition: An alternate path used when the normal route is blocked or unsafe.
keyTerms.example: A truck uses a longer state highway after the primary mountain pass closes.
keyTerms.whyItMatters: A detour only helps when it is safe and has enough capacity for the diverted traffic.

keyTerms.definition: The amount of cargo or traffic that can pass through a route or facility during a period of time.
keyTerms.example: A narrow detour may handle fewer trucks per hour than the closed highway.
keyTerms.whyItMatters: A usable route can still become a bottleneck when demand exceeds its throughput.

keyTerms.definition: A shipment that should move first because a delay could cause greater harm.
keyTerms.example: Temperature-controlled medicine moves before nonessential retail inventory.
keyTerms.whyItMatters: Limited detour capacity should protect health, safety, and essential services first.

question: Which response best protects essential deliveries while the highway is closed?
options: Send every truck to the first available detour without checking capacity
Verify safe detour capacity, prioritize essential loads, and stagger departure times
Hold all deliveries until the original highway reopens
optionRationales: Uncoordinated diversion can overwhelm a smaller road and create another unsafe blockage.
This response verifies the alternate route, protects the most important cargo, and reduces traffic surges.
Holding every shipment avoids the detour but unnecessarily stops essential deliveries that could move safely.
takeaway: An alternate route must be checked for safety and capacity before priority cargo is moved.
responsePrinciple: Verify the detour, protect essential loads, and schedule movement within available capacity.

logisticsEffects.activeReason: The truck stopped before the blocked mountain highway.
logisticsEffects.correctReason: A safe detour and departure window were confirmed for the priority load.
logisticsEffects.incorrectReason: No safe route with available capacity was confirmed.

cascadeSteps: A landslide blocks the primary mountain highway.
Trucks stop or move toward longer alternate roads.
Detour capacity, driver hours, and fuel availability become constrained.
Clinics, stores, farms, and inland communities receive late deliveries.
